title: Universal Crossovers of Stabilizer Entropy Beyond Criticality
authors: Reyhaneh Khasseh, E. A. Ramirez Trino, M. A. Rajabpour
abstract: Stabilizer Rényi entropy has emerged as a probe of nonstabilizerness in quantum many-body systems, but its scaling structure beyond critical points remains poorly understood compared with entanglement entropy. Recent field-theory approaches indicate that stabilizer entropy contains universal critical data and boundary-sensitive terms, raising the question of how these structures extend into massive and crossover regimes. We address this problem for a broad class of finite-range spin chains at Rényi index one-half. We derive exact finite-size formulas for both full periodic chains and finite intervals of the infinite chain, making the universal crossover from critical to noncritical behavior analytically accessible. In periodic geometry, the entropy obeys a volume law away from criticality and exhibits a universal finite-size crossover controlled by the competition between system size and correlation length. We also show that the large-scale SRE density develops a cusp across the field-tuned critical line, while the XX endpoint is governed by a distinct scaling regime associated with the saturation point. In the subsystem geometry, the interval entropy separates bulk critical behavior from boundary contributions generated by the way the finite region cuts the infinite chain. The crossover from critical to massive behavior is then encoded in boundary constants and universal functions controlled by the correlation length. Through exact stabilizer-entropy correspondences, the scaling theory extends to internal XY reductions, Finite-range spin chains, and Cluster--Ising representatives. Our results provide an exact lattice benchmark for the emerging QFT description of stabilizer entropy beyond isolated conformal points.
summary: This paper rigorously calculates the Stabilizer Rényi entropy for solvable spin chains across various physical geometries. By deriving exact finite-size formulas using Pfaffian methods, it establishes a lattice benchmark that precisely maps out how entanglement measures behave when moving away from critical points into massive or crossover regimes.
main_problem: The primary goal is understanding how the scaling structure of Stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) behaves in quantum many-body systems when moving away from critical points into massive or crossover regimes.
main_result: Exact finite-size formulas are derived for SRE in both periodic and subsystem geometries, providing a lattice benchmark that extends QFT descriptions beyond isolated conformal points.
method: The authors use exact solvability techniques applicable to free-fermion spin chains, deriving results via Pfaffian methods and analyzing the factorization properties of correlation matrices across different boundary conditions (periodic vs. interval).
model_or_system: The study focuses on a broad class of finite-range spin chains, particularly the anisotropic XY chain, analyzed in both full periodic geometry (ring) and as an embedded subsystem (interval).
key_observables: Stabilizer Rényi entropy ($	ext{SRE}$), $	ext{Det}_1(G)$ (absolute minor determinant of the correlation matrix), and various scaling functions ($\Phi_{\chi}(\sigma)$).
important_parameters: The anisotropy parameter ($h$), the coupling strength ($\gamma$), system size ($L$ or $\ell$), and the Rényi index ($\alpha=1/2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on specific algebraic structures (Toeplitz/periodic matrices) that allow the intractable absolute-minor problem to be reduced to solvable determinant/Pfaffian forms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate parameter spaces showing critical lines ($h^2 + \gamma^2 = 1$) and compare exact formulas derived for periodic vs. interval geometries, highlighting boundary effects.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes SRE in different physical settings: first the full periodic chain (volume law, cusp), then the subsystem geometry (boundary contributions via Pfaffians), and finally comparing three specific block representations ($	ext{XY}$, $	ext{XYR}$, $	ext{XYL}$) to establish universal scaling laws across regimes.
why_interesting: The work provides rigorous, exact lattice results for a complex entanglement measure (SRE) in critical/crossover regimes, offering crucial benchmarks for theoretical models derived from Quantum Field Theory and CFT.

The lines h = ±1, γ = ±1, and γ = 0, |h| < 1, denote the anisotropic critical, Ising, and critical XX lines, respectively. The zero-field line is special: parity decimation maps (γ, 0) to the TFI point (1,eh), with eh = (1 −γ)/(1 + γ). Arrows denote decimation, Kramers–Wannier duality, and unitary sign equivalences. The marked points organize two orbits. All points within a given orbit have the same SRE, with the appropriate sector or interval-algebra matching.

FIG. 5. Summary of the exact decimation structure and SRE correspondences used throughout the work. A. Periodic chain: correlation matrices decompose into independent G-blocks after site permutations and diagonal gauge transformations, leading to factorization of the generating function and additive SRE. B. Interval subsystem: the same folding acts on Toeplitz truncations, but the endpoints retain the monomial shift, producing ordinary, shifted, and, when ℓ/∈nZ, rectangular blocks; consequently, the determinant sums factorize, and the subsystem SRE becomes additive.
